mechanism_narrative: The recent step-down in WORKPLACES mobility, combined with persistently depressed TRANSIT, reduces weekday trip chaining and in-person shopping. That weakens retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES stays below -25 and TRANSIT stays below -35 in at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and PARKS mobility rises from its trough, households substitute outdoor and home-based activity for shopping trips. This substitution lowers RETAIL_REC within the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a prior week below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after PARKS increases by 5 or more points while RESIDENTIAL remains above 12.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in TRANSIT below its current low signals tougher movement limits or risk avoidance, which directly suppresses discretionary retail trips. The effect appears over a four-week window.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -42 after having been above -42 the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after a TRANSIT break below -42.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve while WORKPLACES remains weak, routine errands replace discretionary shopping and reduce retail-and-recreation visits. The drag should show up within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above -10 and WORKPLACES is below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM stays above -10 and WORKPLACES stays below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT after a mobility trough signals broader willingness to leave home for nonessential trips. That broadening of outside activity should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though PARKS and TRANSIT each improve for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under winter crowd-avoidance conditions, low PARKS mobility paired with weak TRANSIT indicates people are staying close to home rather than visiting retail venues. The retail decline should persist across four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or fails to decline over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining below -20 and RESIDENTIAL above 12.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from its current drop, commuting traffic will spill into nearby retail districts and increase shopping visits. This effect should appear within one week of the rebound.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 4 points week-on-week after a prior week below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after WORKPLACES rises by 4 or more points while TRANSIT is above -45.

mechanism_narrative: A stable or rising GROCERY_PHARM series alongside persistently high RESIDENTIAL suggests household routines are absorbed near home, leaving less time for discretionary retail. That pattern should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -10 and RESIDENTIAL remains above 12.
